Variants.Lore: The crystal hunters of the high peaks work alone and tell no one their clefts. A college of mages pays for mana crystal by the grain.

Vocations.Description: Wins ore, coal and gems from the ground: digs pits and shafts, washes river gravel, follows a vein.
Vocations.Lore: Dangerous work, and free where it is rare: miners held their own courts and laws in many lands. A strike makes a town in a year and an empty one in ten. Miners are clannish and proud and carry tales of what knocks in the dark. Fantasy twists: the dwarven hold, things dug up that should have stayed, ore that only one people can smelt.

Vocations.Name: Quarryman

Variants.Name: quarrier
Variants.Description: Breaks blocks from a rock face with wedges, levers and sledgehammers in an open quarry. Grey with dust, in a leather apron.
Variants.Lore: Quarries are where captives and convicts are sent. A free quarrier wears his own hammer at his belt on feast days, to show which he is.

Variants.Name: stonecutter
Variants.Description: Squares rough blocks to size with a mallet, chisels and a stone axe, in a shed at the quarry or at the building site.
Variants.Lore: Paid by the block, and each block carries his mark so that a bad one can be traced. Dwarves read those marks like signatures.

Variants.Name: slate splitter
Variants.Description: Sits with a block of slate against the knee and splits it into thin roofing sheets with a broad chisel and a mallet.
Variants.Lore: A good splitter gets sixteen sheets from a block and names the sizes after ranks of ladies: queens, duchesses, countesses.

Variants.Name: millstone cutter
Variants.Description: Cuts round millstones from hard gritty rock and dresses their faces with furrows. The finished stones stand on edge, as tall as a person.
Variants.Lore: A stone that cracks on the way down the hill is left where it lies. The hillsides under the old quarries are strewn with them.

Variants.Name: sand digger
Variants.Description: Digs sand from a pit or a river bank with a shovel and carts it to the builders and the glassmakers.
Variants.Lore: A glass town will pay for one pit's sand and refuse the next pit's. The Brinefolk say they can taste the difference.

Variants.Name: gravel digger
Variants.Description: Digs and sieves gravel from river terraces for roads and yards, and loads it into carts with a wide shovel.
Variants.Lore: The Old Realms laid their roads on gravel an arm deep. What a digger does now is mostly patch them.

Variants.Name: clay digger
Variants.Description: Cuts wet clay from a pit with a narrow spade and leaves it in heaps to weather for the potter and the brickmaker.
Variants.Lore: The pits fill with water and become the village ponds. A potter's family and a digger's family are usually the same family.

Vocations.Description: Breaks, splits and dresses stone in an open quarry, and digs sand, gravel and clay.
Vocations.Lore: Heavy, dusty work for the strong and the unfree: quarries are where convicts and captives are sent. A good quarry is known by name, and a cathedral may be built from one hill. Fantasy twists: stone that holds a charm, quarries worked by giants or by the dead.

Vocations.Name: Salter

Variants.Name: salt boiler
Variants.Description: Boils brine in wide lead or iron pans over a fire that never goes out, and rakes the white crust to the side. Stripped to the waist in the steam.
Variants.Lore: A salt town burns a forest every generation. The boilers are paid in salt, and the word for a wage comes from it.

Variants.Name: pan master
Variants.Description: Owns or runs a salt works and judges the moment when the pan is ready to draw. Tastes the brine, and keeps the tally of every basket.
Variants.Lore: The right to a pan is inherited, sold and mortgaged like a house. In a salt town the pan masters are the council.

Variants.Name: salt raker
Variants.Description: Rakes sea salt into white heaps on the clay floors of shallow pans by the shore, under a hot sun. A long wooden rake, a wide hat and bare feet.
Variants.Lore: The Brinefolk rake the flats of their dried sea and hold them in trust until the water comes back. They weep salt, and count that as rent.

Variants.Name: rock-salt miner
Variants.Description: Cuts blocks of grey and pink salt from galleries deep underground and carries them up on the back. The walls glitter in the lamplight.
Variants.Lore: The miners carve chapels, altars and saints out of the salt, deep underground, and are buried from them.

Variants.Name: brine worker
Variants.Description: Draws brine from a well or a spring by bucket and windlass and carries it to the boiling houses in wooden pipes or pails.
Variants.Lore: The well belongs to the town and the brine is shared out by the bucket, by a tally older than the walls.

Variants.Name: soda burner
Variants.Description: Burns seaweed or salt-marsh plants in a pit to a grey cake of soda, for the glassmakers and the soap boilers. Works in bitter smoke on a bare shore.
Variants.Lore: The glass towns buy all the soda a shore can burn. The burners are left with the smoke and a coast without a blade of grass.

Vocations.Description: Makes salt: boils brine, rakes sea salt from pans, cuts rock salt.
Vocations.Lore: Salt is the one thing every house must buy, so rulers tax it and smugglers run it. A salt town is rich, hot and bare, since the pans eat the woods around it. Oaths are sworn on salt. Fantasy twists: a people with salt in the blood, salts that keep the dead from rising.

Vocations.Name: Miller

Variants.Name: water miller
Variants.Description: Keeps a mill on a stream, where a great wooden wheel turns the stones. White with flour, with a sack on the shoulder and a toll dish in the hand.
Variants.Lore: Tenants must grind at the lord's mill and pay the miller his toll, and no one has ever believed the toll dish was honest. The mill pond is where the village drowns its secrets.

Variants.Name: windmill keeper
Variants.Description: Keeps a wooden mill on a hill, turns it to face the wind by its tail pole and sets the cloth on its four sails.
Variants.Lore: A miller sets the sails to a cross for a death and to a slant for a wedding, and the country reads the news from the hill.

Variants.Name: horse-mill keeper
Variants.Description: Grinds where there is no stream and no steady wind: a horse or a donkey walks a circle and turns the stones.
Variants.Lore: Slow and dear, and the only mill a town can keep turning inside its walls in a siege.

Variants.Name: oil presser
Variants.Description: Crushes olives, nuts or seed under a rolling stone and squeezes the mash in a press of beams and screws. The oil runs into jars; everything shines with it.
Variants.Lore: The last pressing lights the lamps and the first goes to the temple. The press house is the one warm place in the village in the cold months, and everyone finds a reason to be there.

Variants.Name: fuller
Variants.Description: Runs a mill whose wheel lifts heavy wooden hammers that pound wet cloth in troughs of water and fuller's earth.
Variants.Lore: The hammers thump day and night and can be heard a valley away. The first machines to put hands out of work, and the first to be broken for it.

Variants.Name: sawyer
Variants.Description: Runs a mill whose wheel drives a saw blade up and down through a log, and stacks the planks to dry.
Variants.Lore: The pit sawyers burned the first sawmills. The mills came back, and the sawyers' sons work in them.

Vocations.Description: Runs a mill: grinds grain to flour and meal, presses oil, and takes a share of what he grinds as toll.
Vocations.Lore: Holds the lord's monopoly, since tenants must grind at the lord's mill, and is suspected by all of a heavy thumb on the scale. The mill stands apart, by the water, and draws tales. The miller is the richest commoner of a village and the least loved. Fantasy twists: a mill that grinds at night for other customers.

Vocations.Name: Baker

Variants.Name: baker
Variants.Description: Kneads dough in a wooden trough before dawn and bakes loaves in a brick oven, drawing them out on a long wooden peel. Floured arms and a white cap.
Variants.Lore: A short loaf earns the baker a ride through the streets with it round his neck. So bakers give thirteen to the dozen, to be safe.

Variants.Name: keeper of the common oven
Variants.Description: Fires the village oven and bakes the dough each household brings, marked with its own sign, for a share of the loaves.
Variants.Lore: Every household's loaf carries its own mark, and the keeper knows by the dough who is doing well and who is stretching the flour.

Variants.Name: pastry cook
Variants.Description: Makes fine things of flour, butter, honey and spice for rich tables: tarts, wafers and gilded cakes. Works with moulds, irons and a light hand.
Variants.Lore: At a feast the pastry is the lord's boast: castles of sugar, pies with live birds. Halflings hold that the pastry cook outranks the knight.

Variants.Name: pie maker
Variants.Description: Bakes meat, fish and fruit in thick crusts and sells the pies hot from a tray in the street.
Variants.Lore: Nobody asks a pie maker what is in the pie. The trade is fined for it every market day and thrives anyway.

Variants.Name: cook
Variants.Description: Cooks for sale: stews in great pots, roasts on a spit, and sells by the bowl and the slice. A stained apron, a ladle and a red face.
Variants.Lore: Halflings rank a cook with a priest. Among the Orcs, who can eat anything, the cook is the one who makes it worth doing.

Variants.Name: cookshop keeper
Variants.Description: Keeps a shop open to the street with a counter and a fire, where those without a kitchen buy a hot meal or bring their own meat to be roasted.
Variants.Lore: Half a town has no hearth of its own and eats from the cookshop. It never closes, and so it hears everything.

Vocations.Description: Turns flour into bread and other cooked food for sale, and bakes the dough that households bring to the common oven.
Vocations.Lore: The most watched trade in a town. The weight and price of the loaf are fixed by law, and a baker who cheats is paraded with the loaf round his neck. Up before dawn. Bread riots start at the baker's door.

Vocations.Name: Brewer

Variants.Name: brewer
Variants.Description: Mashes malt in hot water in a great tun, boils the wort with hops or herbs and ferments it in open vats. Works in steam, with a long wooden paddle.
Variants.Lore: Dwarves brew strong and keep the yeast of a hold alive for centuries: a brewer who loses it is remembered by name. Monks brew the best ale and say it is for the guests.

Variants.Name: alewife
Variants.Description: A woman who brews ale in her own kitchen and sells it at the door, with a bush on a pole outside when a new brew is ready.
Variants.Lore: The ale taster calls unannounced and fines her either way: for weak ale, or for a short measure. The fine is a licence under another name.

Variants.Name: maltster
Variants.Description: Soaks barley, spreads it on a floor to sprout and dries it over a kiln, turning it with a wooden shovel.
Variants.Lore: A malt kiln burns down oftener than any other building in a town. The maltster lives beside it and sleeps lightly.

Variants.Name: wine maker
Variants.Description: Treads grapes in a vat, presses the skins and keeps the wine in barrels in a cool cellar. Legs stained purple at the vintage.
Variants.Lore: Elves lay down a vintage for a guest who is not yet born. Everyone else drinks the wine within the year, before it turns.

Variants.Name: cider maker
Variants.Description: Crushes apples in a stone trough under a rolling wheel and presses the pulp between layers of straw.
Variants.Lore: Halflings pay a harvest hand part of the wage in cider and take the quality of both seriously.

Variants.Name: mead maker
Variants.Description: Ferments honey and water in crocks, plain or with herbs and fruit. A golden drink for feasts and halls.
Variants.Lore: The drink of the Northmen's halls. An oath sworn over the mead horn binds as hard as one sworn on iron.

Variants.Name: distiller
Variants.Description: Heats wine or mash in a copper still and catches the strong spirit that drips from its beak. Half brewer, half alchemist.
Variants.Lore: The alchemists called it the water of life and sold it as medicine. The Gnomes made the still that made it a drink.

Vocations.Description: Makes drink: malts and brews ale and beer, presses and ferments wine and cider, makes mead.
Vocations.Lore: In the country brewing is women's by-work in every second house, and the ale-stake over the door is the first inn. In towns it becomes a trade, and in monasteries an art. Drink is safer than water and is wages, medicine and sacrament. Fantasy twists: dwarven beer, halfling cider, a vintage that remembers.

Vocations.Name: Butcher

Variants.Name: butcher
Variants.Description: Cuts up carcasses on a heavy block and sells meat from an open stall hung with joints. A cleaver, a knife steel and a bloody apron.
Variants.Lore: Butchers are rich, armed with their tools and quick to riot, and no council crosses their guild lightly. They may not serve on a jury in a trial for blood.

Variants.Name: slaughterer
Variants.Description: Kills cattle, sheep and pigs with a poleaxe and a knife, bleeds them and skins them. Works in a yard by running water.
Variants.Lore: Kept outside the walls and downstream by law. In some faiths the slaughterer must be a priest, and in others he may never enter the temple.

Variants.Name: poulterer
Variants.Description: Sells hens, geese, ducks and game birds, alive in wicker cages or plucked and hung by the feet.
Variants.Lore: The goose girl and the poulterer's wife are the gossips of every tale. Feathers go to the fletcher and the bedmaker, and nothing is wasted.

Variants.Name: tripe seller
Variants.Description: Washes and boils the stomachs, feet and heads the butcher cannot sell, and sells them cheap and hot from a tub.
Variants.Lore: The food of the poor and of the morning after. Orcs say a people that will not eat tripe has never been hungry.

Variants.Name: fishmonger
Variants.Description: Sells fish from a wet stone slab or a barrel: fresh from the boats, or salted, smoked and dried from far away.
Variants.Lore: On fast days the fishmonger is the richest man in the market. The fishwives' tongue is a byword in every port.

Variants.Name: fish salter
Variants.Description: Guts fish and packs them in barrels between layers of salt, or hangs them in a smokehouse. Hands cracked by brine.
Variants.Lore: A barrel of herring is sealed with the town's brand, and a false brand costs the salter a hand.

Variants.Name: pickler
Variants.Description: Keeps meat, fish and greens in brine, vinegar and spice, in rows of crocks and casks.
Variants.Lore: Halfling cellars got them through the Ashen Years, and the pickler is honoured for it at every harvest feast.

Variants.Name: renderer
Variants.Description: Boils fat, bones and scraps in great cauldrons for tallow, lard, glue and oil. A foul trade at the edge of town.
Variants.Lore: The trade nobody will live beside and no one can do without. Hoarkin render blubber on the ice, where the smell offends no one but the bears.

Variants.Name: tallow chandler
Variants.Description: Dips wicks again and again into hot tallow until they are candles, and hangs them in rows on a rack to harden.
Variants.Lore: Tallow for the house, wax for the temple. The two chandlers' guilds have been at law for longer than either can prove.

Variants.Name: soap boiler
Variants.Description: Boils fat with lye from wood ash in an iron kettle, stirs for hours and cuts the cooled soap into bars.
Variants.Lore: Soap is a town luxury; the country uses lye and sand. The Stillfaces, who speak by scent, will not let a scented soap into the house.

Vocations.Description: Slaughters and cuts up animals and sells the meat, and deals with all that an animal or a fish leaves: salts and smokes it, renders the fat.
Vocations.Lore: A rich and rough trade, kept to its own street and banned from fouling the river. Butchers are strong, armed with their tools and quick to riot, and town councils fear them. Blood and offal give the trade a taint that money does not wash off.

Vocations.Name: Charcoal burner

Variants.Name: collier
Variants.Description: Stacks wood into a round mound, covers it with turf and lets it smoulder for days, watching day and night from a hut beside it. Black with soot.
Variants.Lore: Sits on a one-legged stool, so that he falls and wakes if he dozes while the clamp burns. Outlaws and lost children are both said to be safe at a collier's fire.

Variants.Name: tar burner
Variants.Description: Burns resinous pine roots in a covered pit on a slope and catches the black tar that runs out at the bottom in barrels.
Variants.Lore: Northmen tar their ships, their roofs and their ropes, and a district pays its tax in barrels. The pits can be smelt from the sea.

Variants.Name: pitch boiler
Variants.Description: Boils tar down in an iron cauldron until it is thick black pitch, for ships, barrels and torches.
Variants.Lore: A pitch kettle that catches takes the yard with it. Shipwrights keep the boilers at the far end of the beach.

Variants.Name: ash burner
Variants.Description: Burns hardwood to ash, washes the ash with water and boils the lye dry for potash, in iron pots in the forest.
Variants.Lore: It takes a great tree to make a small pot of potash. The glassmakers and the soap boilers pay, and the forest does not come back.

Variants.Name: varnish maker
Variants.Description: Melts resins and amber with oil in a small pot over a careful fire, and sells the clear varnish to painters and joiners.
Variants.Lore: Amberbloods make the best varnish and will not say what is in it. The other peoples have a guess, and do not ask.

Variants.Name: lime burner
Variants.Description: Burns limestone in a stone kiln on a hillside and draws out white quicklime for mortar. Wrapped in cloth against the burning dust.
Variants.Lore: The kiln's fumes kill a sleeper beside it, and tramps who lie down by a warm kiln are found there in the morning.

Vocations.Description: Turns wood into the fuels and stuffs that industry needs, by slow fire in the forest: charcoal, tar, pitch, potash, and lime from limestone.
Vocations.Lore: Lives in the wood by the smoking clamp for weeks, black, poor and seldom seen in the village, and is suspected of dealing with whatever else lives there. Outlaws hide among charcoal burners. Without them no iron is made.

Vocations.Name: Smelter

Variants.Name: bloomery man
Variants.Description: Smelts iron in a clay furnace the height of a person, working the bellows for hours, and draws out a glowing spongy lump to hammer.
Variants.Lore: Sunlanders were the first to smelt iron. The furnace is built like a woman giving birth, and the smelters keep apart from their wives while it burns.

Variants.Name: iron smelter
Variants.Description: Roasts and smelts iron ore with charcoal and sells the metal in bars. A leather apron, long tongs and arms scarred by sparks.
Variants.Lore: The works follow the wood. A valley is smelted bare in a generation, and the smelters move on and leave a name with hammer in it.

Variants.Name: furnace master
Variants.Description: Runs a great furnace blown by water-driven bellows and commands its crew. Judges the heat by the colour of the flame, and taps the molten metal.
Variants.Lore: Reads the flame through a hole the size of a coin and is paid more than the lord's steward. Hearthbloods stand closer to the tap than anyone else can.

Variants.Name: copper smelter
Variants.Description: Roasts green and grey copper ore on open heaps and smelts it to red metal. The smoke kills the trees around the works.
Variants.Lore: The ground round the roasting heaps stays bare for a lifetime. The smelters are short-lived and well paid, and know the bargain.

Variants.Name: silver refiner
Variants.Description: Melts silver-bearing lead on a hearth of bone ash and blows air across it until a bright button of silver is left.
Variants.Lore: Works under the eye of the ruler's assayer. What is left in the hearth belongs to the refiner, and refiners have grown rich on sweepings.

Variants.Name: steel maker
Variants.Description: Bakes iron with charcoal in sealed clay pots until it becomes steel, by a recipe passed from parent to child.
Variants.Lore: The Rainkeepers make the watered steel that every swordsmith wants, and are born into the work. The recipe has never been written down.

Variants.Name: bronze founder
Variants.Description: Melts copper and tin together in a crucible and pours the bronze into ingots, at the works where the ore is smelted.
Variants.Lore: Bronze was the metal of the Dawn. The founders say iron is a fashion, and are still waiting.

Vocations.Description: Turns ore into metal: roasts, smelts and refines it in a furnace, and casts or hammers it into bars.
Vocations.Lore: A secret art. The smelter knows by the colour of the flame when the bloom is ready, and passes that on to a son only. In many peoples the smelter is a ritual figure, feared and set apart. The works move when the wood is gone.

Vocations.Name: Tanner

Variants.Name: tanner
Variants.Description: Soaks hides in pits of lime and oak bark for months and scrapes them over a beam with a two-handled knife. Stained brown, and smelt from afar.
Variants.Lore: Banished downstream and downwind. Tanners marry tanners, and the saying is that nothing gets the smell out but a second fortune.

Variants.Name: tawyer
Variants.Description: Makes soft white leather with alum, salt and egg yolk instead of bark, for gloves and fine goods.
Variants.Lore: White leather for the gloves of the rich. The tawyers hold themselves above the tanners and are kept to the same end of town.

Variants.Name: currier
Variants.Description: Finishes tanned leather: shaves it even, works in oil and tallow and stretches it until it is supple and coloured.
Variants.Lore: A hide is no use until the currier has had it, and the shoemakers hate paying for that. The two guilds share a street and not a word.

Variants.Name: skinner
Variants.Description: Flays carcasses and trades in raw hides and pelts, salted and bundled.
Variants.Lore: The skinner takes the dead horse and the dog nobody claims. In some towns he is also the hangman's man.

Variants.Name: furrier
Variants.Description: Dresses pelts with the hair on and matches them into linings and trims. A rich trade with soft hands, among hanging furs.
Variants.Lore: The law says who may wear which fur, and the furrier knows who breaks it. As rich as a mercer, and never quite as welcome.

Variants.Name: parchment maker
Variants.Description: Stretches limed calf and sheep skins on a wooden frame and scrapes them thin with a moon-shaped knife, until they are smooth white sheets.
Variants.Lore: A book takes a flock. The parchment maker counts a library in sheep, and sells the best skins to the Lanternkin for their contracts.

Vocations.Description: Makes leather, fur and parchment from raw hides and pelts, by months of soaking in lime, bark and worse.
Vocations.Lore: The foulest trade in a town, banished downstream and downwind, and its people marry among themselves. Yet leather is in every shoe, saddle, belt and book, and furs are the mark of rank. The furriers are rich where the tanners are shunned.

Vocations.Name: Weaver

Variants.Name: spinner
Variants.Description: Spins wool or flax to thread with a distaff and a drop spindle, or at a wheel. Mostly a woman, and spinning at every idle moment.
Variants.Lore: Every woman spins, and the law calls an unmarried one by the name of the work. It takes eight spinners to keep one weaver at the loom.

Variants.Name: weaver
Variants.Description: Sits at a wooden loom, throws the shuttle through the warp and beats the cloth tight. A cramped workshop with a window for light.
Variants.Lore: Weavers think while they work, and think the same things: the weavers' quarter is where every heresy and every rising begins.

Variants.Name: linen weaver
Variants.Description: Weaves fine linen from flax thread in a damp cellar, where the thread does not snap, and bleaches the cloth on the grass.
Variants.Lore: Works in a damp cellar and coughs from it. The poorest of the weavers, and the proverb makes him the least honest.

Variants.Name: silk weaver
Variants.Description: Weaves patterned silk on a tall loom, with a helper perched above to pull the pattern cords. The richest cloth, for court and temple.
Variants.Lore: A master's pattern is the family's fortune. A weaver who carries it out of the town has put a price on his own head.

Variants.Name: fuller
Variants.Description: Treads new woollen cloth in a trough of water, stale urine and fuller's earth to clean and thicken it. Bare legs and a strong smell.
Variants.Lore: The fullers walk the cloth and sing to keep time. No one sits near them in the tavern, and they have stopped minding.

Variants.Name: dyer
Variants.Description: Boils cloth and yarn in vats of colour and lifts them out on poles, with arms stained to the elbow.
Variants.Lore: Known by the hands. The dyer of red and the dyer of blue are separate guilds and may not touch each other's vats. Boughwalkers dye in a colour that no one else can see.

Variants.Name: shearman
Variants.Description: Raises the nap of finished cloth with teasels and crops it smooth with shears as long as an arm.
Variants.Lore: The last hand on the cloth and the one that can ruin it. A shearman's shears are his own and are buried with him.

Variants.Name: felt maker
Variants.Description: Lays wet wool in layers and rolls, beats and treads it into felt, for hats, boots, rugs and tents.
Variants.Lore: The Grass riders live under felt, walk on it and are buried in it. The felt for a new tent is rolled by the whole camp.

Variants.Name: carpet weaver
Variants.Description: Knots coloured wool onto an upright loom, row by row, from a pattern held in the head, and trims the pile with shears.
Variants.Lore: A carpet takes a year and tells who made it: every people ties its own knot. The makers leave one fault in on purpose, since only a god's work is whole.

Variants.Name: rope maker
Variants.Description: Walks backwards down a long ropewalk paying out hemp from a bundle at the waist, while a wheel twists the strands into rope.
Variants.Lore: The ropewalk is the longest building in a port. The hangman buys there, and the rope maker does not ask which coil.

Variants.Name: net maker
Variants.Description: Knots twine into fishing and fowling nets with a flat wooden needle and a mesh gauge, and mends torn ones by the harbour.
Variants.Lore: Old sailors and fishers' widows mend nets on the quay. The Shoalfolk tie a knot into each net that names the family.

Vocations.Description: Makes cloth and cordage from fibre and wool: spins, weaves, fulls, dyes and finishes.
Vocations.Lore: The first industry, and the first to split master from hand. Spinning is done in every cottage, mostly by women; weaving is a guild trade; the dyers and fullers are its foul end, the cloth merchants its rich one. Weavers' quarters are crowded, radical and quick to strike. Fantasy twists: cloth that hides its wearer, dyes that only one people can see.

Vocations.Name: Smith

Variants.Name: blacksmith
Variants.Description: Heats iron in a charcoal forge and hammers it on an anvil. A leather apron, bare forearms, tongs and a hammer, in a dark smithy lit by the fire.
Variants.Lore: Every village needs one and half fear theirs. The smith pulls teeth, binds oaths on the anvil and, in the far north, marries couples over it.

Variants.Name: farrier
Variants.Description: Shoes horses: pares the hoof, fits the hot shoe in a hiss of smoke and nails it on. Also doctors the horse.
Variants.Lore: A horseshoe over the door keeps luck in, points up. The farrier is the horse's physician and often the village's too.

Variants.Name: toolsmith
Variants.Description: Forges edged tools: axes, scythes, chisels and spades, with a strip of steel welded into the edge.
Variants.Lore: Dwarven tools carry a maker's mark and a warranty of a lifetime, and the Dwarves mean a Dwarf's lifetime.

Variants.Name: nailer
Variants.Description: Makes nails all day at a small forge: heats a rod, points it, cuts it and heads it with a few blows. Poor piece-work.
Variants.Lore: The poorest of those who work iron: whole families at one small forge, paid by the thousand. A nailer's child can make a nail before it can read.

Variants.Name: cutler
Variants.Description: Makes knives, shears and razors, grinds them on a wheel and fits the handles of horn, bone and wood.
Variants.Lore: A knife carries its town's mark, and a town will go to war over a forged one. Everyone eats with their own knife and is judged by it.

Variants.Name: locksmith
Variants.Description: Files locks, keys, hinges and iron-bound strongboxes at a bench, with small tools and a vice.
Variants.Lore: Sworn never to make a key from a wax print or for a stranger. The oath is taken before the whole guild, and broken in private.

Variants.Name: weaponsmith
Variants.Description: Forges swords, spearheads and axes, and hardens them in oil or water. The blades are tested and marked with the maker's stamp.
Variants.Lore: A sword has a name and a lineage, and its smith is remembered with it. Some smiths will not sell to a man they dislike the look of.

Variants.Name: armourer
Variants.Description: Hammers plates of steel over stakes and rounded anvils into helmets and harness, and rivets mail ring by ring.
Variants.Lore: Dwarves fit a harness to the man like a tailor and keep his measures on file, with his debts.

Variants.Name: sword polisher
Variants.Description: Grinds and polishes finished blades on stones of ever finer grit until the steel shines, and fits hilt and scabbard.
Variants.Lore: The polisher sees what the smith hid: every flaw comes up under the stone. The guild is larger than the swordsmiths', and prouder.

Variants.Name: bronze founder
Variants.Description: Casts bronze and brass in moulds of clay and wax in a town workshop: pots, buckles, statues and fittings.
Variants.Lore: Sunlanders cast the heads of their kings in bronze, and the founders are a caste that serves the palace alone.

Variants.Name: bell caster
Variants.Description: Casts great bells in a pit dug beside the temple that ordered them, and tunes each by chipping metal from its rim.
Variants.Lore: A bell is cast at night, beside the tower it is for, with the whole town watching. People throw in silver for the tone, and the caster lets them.

Variants.Name: forge hand
Variants.Description: Works the bellows, feeds the fire and swings the sledgehammer to the smith's tap. Sweating, in a scorched apron.
Variants.Lore: Hearthbloods work the fire bare-armed where others need tongs and leather, and Dwarven holds hire them by the company.

Vocations.Description: Works hot metal with hammer and anvil: makes and mends tools, shoes horses, and in a town forges blades, locks, nails and armour.
Vocations.Lore: The one craftsman every village must have, and the one most wrapped in tale: fire, iron and a strength that seems more than natural. The smithy is where news is traded. In a city the trade splits into a dozen guilds that quarrel over who may make what. Fantasy twists: the smith who forges under a ban or a blessing, rune blades, a people whose smiths are its priests.

Vocations.Name: Carpenter

Variants.Name: carpenter
Variants.Description: Hews beams with an axe and an adze and joins them with pegs into house frames, roofs and barns. Carries a saw, an auger and a chalk line.
Variants.Lore: A house frame is cut on the ground, every joint numbered, and raised in a day by the whole village. A green bough is nailed to the ridge, and the owner pays in ale.

Variants.Name: joiner
Variants.Description: Makes fine fitted work at a bench with planes and chisels: doors, panelling, tables and benches, without a nail.
Variants.Lore: The carpenters say a joiner is a carpenter afraid of heights. The joiners say a carpenter is a joiner who cannot measure.

Variants.Name: wheelwright
Variants.Description: Builds wheels: a turned hub, oak spokes, curved rim pieces, and an iron tyre shrunk on hot.
Variants.Lore: A wheel is the hardest thing a village makes. Tyring day needs the smith, a fire in the yard and every hand that can hold a bucket.

Variants.Name: cartwright
Variants.Description: Builds carts and wagons: frame, axle, shafts and boards, with the wheelwright's wheels.
Variants.Lore: Every district builds its own cart, and a stranger's home can be told from his wagon before he speaks.

Variants.Name: cooper
Variants.Description: Shapes staves, bends them over a fire and binds them with hoops into barrels, tubs and buckets that hold water.
Variants.Lore: A barrel is the measure of trade, and the cooper's mark is the warrant that it holds what it should. An apprentice is rolled in his first barrel.

Variants.Name: turner
Variants.Description: Turns bowls, cups, spindles and chair legs on a lathe worked by a foot treadle and a springy pole.
Variants.Lore: Turners work in the woods where the timber stands, through the summer, and come to the fair with a cartload of bowls.

Variants.Name: chest maker
Variants.Description: Makes chests and coffers of boards, bound with iron and often carved or painted: the main furniture of every house.
Variants.Lore: A bride brings her chest and a dead man leaves his. Whoever holds the key to the chest holds the house.

Variants.Name: bowyer
Variants.Description: Shapes bow staves of yew, ash or elm with a drawknife, or glues horn, wood and sinew into short recurved bows.
Variants.Lore: Elves season a stave for longer than a human bowyer lives. The Grass riders glue horn and sinew, and take a year over a bow they will not sell.

Variants.Name: fletcher
Variants.Description: Makes arrows: straightens the shafts, glues and binds on goose feathers, and fits the iron heads.
Variants.Lore: The king takes six feathers from every goose in time of war. A fletcher counts the peace in geese.

Variants.Name: sled maker
Variants.Description: Builds sleds and sledges of bent wood lashed with hide, without nails, for snow and ice.
Variants.Lore: The Hoarkin build without iron, because iron snaps in the cold, and lash with hide so that the sled gives on rough ice.

Variants.Name: woodcarver
Variants.Description: Carves figures, leaves and beasts into beams, doors, ship prows and furniture, with gouges and a mallet.
Variants.Lore: Amberbloods carve only wood that fell by itself. The Northmen put a beast's head on the prow and take it off in sight of land, so as not to frighten the spirits there.

Vocations.Description: Works wood into buildings, vehicles, vessels and tools.
Vocations.Lore: The builder of the common world: house frames, carts, barrels, looms and mills are all his. A master carpenter raises a hall with a crew and a rope. Less secret than the smith and less grand than the mason, and found everywhere. The cooper's barrel is the shipping container of the age.

Vocations.Name: Shipwright

Variants.Name: shipwright
Variants.Description: Builds seagoing ships on a slipway by eye, without drawings: keel, ribs and planking, with an adze, an axe and an auger.
Variants.Lore: Built by eye and by a rule of thumb passed down in the family. Northmen name the ship at the keel-laying, and once put more than a name under the keel.

Variants.Name: boatbuilder
Variants.Description: Builds small craft on the beach: rowing boats, fishing boats and skiffs, of overlapping planks riveted together.
Variants.Lore: Every shore has its own boat, shaped by its own surf. The Shoalfolk are born in one and build their first before they marry.

Variants.Name: caulker
Variants.Description: Drives tarred hemp into the seams of a hull with a caulking iron and a mallet, and seals them with hot pitch.
Variants.Lore: The sound of the mallets is how a port knows its yard is in work. The space between the planks is called the devil, and the caulker pays him.

Variants.Name: hull mender
Variants.Description: Repairs ships in harbour: patches sprung planks, scrapes weed and shell from the bottom, and where the mender can dive, works under the water.
Variants.Lore: Shoalfolk menders work under water on one breath and are hired in every harbour, though no land law reaches them and no harbour master likes it.

Variants.Name: sail maker
Variants.Description: Sews strips of heavy canvas into sails in a wide loft, with a three-sided needle and a leather palm, and ropes their edges.
Variants.Lore: A sail loft is the largest dry floor in a port, so it is also where the town dances. Winds, where they can be bought, are sewn into a hem.

Variants.Name: barge builder
Variants.Description: Builds flat-bottomed barges and lighters for rivers and canals, wide and shallow, to carry grain, stone and timber.
Variants.Lore: The Halflings' river barges are homes as much as boats, and a builder is paid part of the price in dinners aboard.

Vocations.Description: Builds and repairs boats and ships.
Vocations.Lore: A ship is the largest machine the age can build, and the yard that builds it is a town's pride and its debt. The craft is by eye and by inheritance, with no drawings. Launches are blessed, and a ship has a name and a luck. Fantasy twists: keels of elder wood, hulls sung into shape.

Vocations.Name: Mason

Variants.Name: stonemason
Variants.Description: Cuts stone to a line with a mallet and chisels and lays it true with plumb line, square and level. Dusty, in a leather apron, with his mark on every block.
Variants.Lore: Masons travel to where the great works are, lodge together and know each other by signs. What the lodge teaches is geometry, and what it keeps is silence.

Variants.Name: bricklayer
Variants.Description: Lays brick in courses with a trowel and mortar along a stretched line, on a scaffold of poles.
Variants.Lore: The masons call brick the poor man's stone. The bricklayers answer that half the cities of the Old Realms are brick and still standing.

Variants.Name: builder
Variants.Description: Takes on a whole building for a price and brings the crew: reads the ground, sets out the walls with pegs and cord, and oversees the work.
Variants.Lore: A builder who has never had a wall fall has not built enough, the saying goes. The contract names a penalty for each week late, and each week is late.

Variants.Name: plasterer
Variants.Description: Coats walls and ceilings with lime plaster from a board, with a trowel and a float, and whitewashes them.
Variants.Lore: A fresh wall waits for the painter. A plasterer who puts a hand to it himself is fined by the painters' guild.

Variants.Name: tiler
Variants.Description: Lays clay tiles on roofs and floors, pegging or bedding each one. Works on the roof with a tile hammer.
Variants.Lore: After a town burns, the council orders tile for every roof, and the tilers are rich until the order is forgotten.

Variants.Name: roofer
Variants.Description: Covers roofs with slate, wooden shingles or lead sheet. Works high on the laths with a pick-hammer and a pouch of nails.
Variants.Lore: Roofers drink more than other builders, by repute, and fall less than the repute would suggest.

Variants.Name: thatcher
Variants.Description: Lays bundles of reed or straw on a roof, pins them with hazel rods and combs them smooth with a toothed rake.
Variants.Lore: Each thatcher finishes the ridge with a knot or a straw beast of his own, and a village can name the man from the roof.

Variants.Name: steeplejack
Variants.Description: Climbs towers and spires on ropes and ladders to mend what no scaffold reaches. Light, sure-footed and without fear of height.
Variants.Lore: Boughwalkers and Catfolk hold the trade in most cities. They are paid by the height, and the spire's weathercock is theirs to set.

Variants.Name: well digger
Variants.Description: Digs a round shaft down to water and lines it with stone as it goes, hauled up and down in a bucket.
Variants.Lore: Paid on water, not on depth. A dry shaft is the digger's loss, so diggers and dowsers work in pairs and blame each other.

Variants.Name: bridge builder
Variants.Description: Builds bridges: drives piles in the river bed, raises piers, and turns stone arches over timber frames.
Variants.Lore: The first to cross a new bridge belongs to the devil, the tale says, so a dog or a cock is sent over. Building one is a pious work that wipes out sins.

Variants.Name: engineer
Variants.Description: Plans great works with compass, rule and model: walls, canals, harbours and aqueducts. A master in a long gown, with drawings and a measuring rod.
Variants.Lore: Dwarven engineers sign a wall and answer for it for a hundred years. The Canal folk examine theirs before they let them touch a dike.

Vocations.Description: Builds in stone, brick and earth: cuts and lays stone, burns and lays brick, plasters, tiles and thatches, and plans works such as walls, bridges, wells and canals.
Vocations.Lore: The travelling aristocracy of the crafts. Masons go where the great works are, lodge together on the site, and keep their geometry to themselves. A master mason is architect and contractor in one. Fantasy twists: lodges with real secrets, dwarven stonework that needs no mortar, walls with something bound into the foundation.

Vocations.Name: Potter

Variants.Name: potter
Variants.Description: Throws pots on a wheel turned by the foot, with wet hands. Rows of grey pots dry on boards before they go to the kiln.
Variants.Lore: Potters leave more behind than kings do. In many faiths the first people were thrown on a wheel, and the potter says so when the price is questioned.

Variants.Name: brickmaker
Variants.Description: Presses clay into wooden moulds, turns the bricks out in rows to dry and fires them in a great stacked clamp.
Variants.Lore: A season's work, from the last frost to the first. The clamp burns for weeks, and its smoke marks the edge of every growing town.

Variants.Name: tile maker
Variants.Description: Shapes roof and floor tiles in moulds or over the thigh, and fires them in a kiln. Floor tiles are stamped with patterns.
Variants.Lore: The tile works belong to the temple or the lord more often than to the maker. A paw print in a tile is left in, for luck.

Variants.Name: kiln master
Variants.Description: Stacks the kiln, feeds the fire for days and judges the heat by its colour through a spy hole. One mistake spoils the whole load.
Variants.Lore: The kiln is opened at dawn with the whole pottery standing by. A god of the kiln has an altar on it, and gets the first pot or the blame.

Variants.Name: maker of fine ware
Variants.Description: Makes thin, glazed and painted ware for rich tables, white-bodied or lustred, by a recipe that is the town's secret.
Variants.Lore: The Canal folk kept the white ware to themselves for centuries. Courts elsewhere locked up alchemists until they found the recipe.

Vocations.Description: Shapes and fires clay: pots, bowls and jars, bricks and roof tiles.
Vocations.Lore: A humble and ancient trade that leaves more behind than any other. Potters work at the edge of town, where the clay and the fire risk are. A fine ware (a glaze, a white body) can make a town's name and is a guarded recipe.

Vocations.Name: Glassmaker

Variants.Name: glassblower
Variants.Description: Gathers molten glass on the end of an iron pipe, blows it into a bubble and shapes it with tongs, at the mouth of a roaring furnace.
Variants.Lore: A glass town forbids its masters to leave and hunts those who do. In return they may marry into the nobility, and their furnaces never go out.

Variants.Name: glazier
Variants.Description: Cuts panes of coloured and clear glass and sets them in strips of lead to make windows.
Variants.Lore: Coloured windows are the books of those who cannot read. The glazier signs with a small figure of himself in a corner, kneeling.

Variants.Name: bead maker
Variants.Description: Winds threads of molten glass round an iron rod over a lamp flame to make beads, in every colour.
Variants.Lore: Beads are the coin of the long trade: a string buys ivory, gold or a guide where no one takes silver.

Variants.Name: mirror maker
Variants.Description: Backs flat or blown glass with tin and quicksilver, or polishes a disc of bronze, to make a mirror.
Variants.Lore: The quicksilver takes the maker's teeth, then his wits. A mirror is covered in a house of mourning, and a mage will pay for one that was never looked into.

Variants.Name: lens grinder
Variants.Description: Grinds discs of glass or rock crystal against a curved dish with sand and water into reading stones and spectacle lenses.
Variants.Lore: Gnomes ground the first spectacles and gave scholars twenty more years of reading. The scholars have not agreed whether to thank them.

Variants.Name: vial blower
Variants.Description: Blows small thin vessels at a lamp: vials, flasks and tubes for apothecaries, alchemists and mages. Fine work for steady breath.
Variants.Lore: Lanternkin blow the vials that hold their own blood for a contract: it glows as long as the signer lives.

Vocations.Description: Melts sand or crystal with a flux and blows, casts or grinds the glass.
Vocations.Lore: A prized and jealous art. Glass towns forbid their masters to leave, on pain of death in the tale. Window glass is for temples and the rich; a lens is a wonder. The furnaces never go out. Fantasy twists: glass that holds light, a scrying mirror, vials that keep a living flame.

Vocations.Name: Leatherworker

Variants.Name: shoemaker
Variants.Description: Cuts and sews new shoes and boots at a low bench in an open stall, with an awl, waxed thread and wooden lasts.
Variants.Lore: The shoemaker thinks while he sews and talks while he fits, and every rising has a shoemaker in it. His own children go barefoot, by the proverb.

Variants.Name: cobbler
Variants.Description: Mends old shoes and remakes them for resale: patches, new soles and heels. Poorer than the shoemaker, with a bench in the street.
Variants.Lore: The guilds have fought for centuries over how much new leather a cobbler may put in an old shoe. The cobbler is told to stick to his last, and does not.

Variants.Name: saddler
Variants.Description: Builds saddles over a wooden tree, padded and covered with leather, tooled and studded for those who can pay.
Variants.Lore: A Grass rider is measured for a saddle once and rides it for life, and is buried on it.

Variants.Name: harness maker
Variants.Description: Cuts and stitches straps, collars, bridles and traces for draught and riding animals, and fits the buckles.
Variants.Lore: A broken trace stops a harvest. The harness maker's lamp burns latest in the weeks before it.

Variants.Name: girdler
Variants.Description: Makes belts and girdles of leather and cloth, set with metal mounts, studs and buckles.
Variants.Lore: A belt shows rank by its mounts, and the law says who may wear silver ones. A woman's keys hang from it, and a man's knife.

Variants.Name: glover
Variants.Description: Cuts gloves from soft thin leather with shears and sews them with tiny stitches, plain, embroidered or perfumed.
Variants.Lore: A glove thrown down is a challenge, a glove given is a pledge, and a glove sent is a summons. Glovers scent them, and poisoners have learnt from glovers.

Variants.Name: purse maker
Variants.Description: Makes purses, pouches and bags that hang from the belt, of leather and cloth with drawstrings and clasps.
Variants.Lore: The purse maker and the cutpurse know each other's work well. The strongest strings are sold with a wink.

Variants.Name: scabbard maker
Variants.Description: Makes sheaths for swords and knives: thin wood covered with leather, with a metal tip and mouth.
Variants.Lore: The sword gets the name, and the scabbard gets the rain. A blade drawn from another man's scabbard is bad luck.

Variants.Name: bookbinder
Variants.Description: Covers the wooden boards of a book in leather and decorates it with stamps, tooling, bosses and clasps.
Variants.Lore: A book is bound to outlast its owner and chained to outlast the thief. The clasp matters: parchment swells if it is not held shut.

Vocations.Description: Makes goods of leather: shoes above all, and saddles, harness, belts, gloves, purses, sheaths and bottles.
Vocations.Lore: The most numerous craft in any town, since shoes wear out. The shoemaker in his open stall hears and repeats everything, and is the proverbial town philosopher and radical. Shoemakers of new leather and cobblers of old fight over the line between them.

Vocations.Name: Tailor

Variants.Name: tailor
Variants.Description: Measures with a strip of parchment, cuts the cloth with great shears and sews sitting cross-legged on the table. A needle, a thimble and chalk.
Variants.Lore: Nine tailors make a man, the insult goes. But the tailor knows every measure, every debt and every thickening waist in town.

Variants.Name: seamstress
Variants.Description: A woman who sews linen: shirts, shifts, sheets and caps, with fine even stitches, at home or in a workroom.
Variants.Lore: Paid by the piece, and poorly. A girl's sampler shows her stitches to a mistress, and a seamstress's eyes last twenty years.

Variants.Name: robe maker
Variants.Description: Makes the long gowns of office and ceremony for priests, judges, scholars and mages, in rich cloth with wide sleeves.
Variants.Lore: The cut and colour of a gown are law: a judge, a doctor and a mage may each be known at a hundred paces, and may not dress otherwise.

Variants.Name: hosier
Variants.Description: Cuts and sews close-fitting hose from cloth cut on the slant, or knits stockings.
Variants.Lore: Parti-coloured hose in a lord's colours mark his men. The preachers call tight hose a sin, and the hosiers thank them for the custom.

Variants.Name: hatter
Variants.Description: Shapes felt over wooden blocks with steam into hats, and trims them with bands, brooches and feathers.
Variants.Lore: A hat is doffed, and to whom is the whole of manners. Hatters go strange from the fumes of the felt, and it is said without malice.

Variants.Name: embroiderer
Variants.Description: Works pictures and patterns in silk and gold thread on cloth stretched in a frame, for vestments, banners and court dress.
Variants.Lore: Vestments worth more than the church they hang in. The gold thread is weighed out to the embroiderer and weighed back.

Variants.Name: garment furrier
Variants.Description: Lines and trims clothes with fur: sews small pelts into a lining and fits it to gown, hood and cloak.
Variants.Lore: A lining can be worth more than the gown and is unpicked to be left in a will. The belly fur of the squirrel is counted by the thousand.

Variants.Name: old-clothes dealer
Variants.Description: Buys worn clothes, mends and turns them, and sells them again from a stall hung thick with garments.
Variants.Lore: Most people never wear a new coat. In a plague year the dealers are rich, and are blamed for the next street that falls sick.

Vocations.Description: Cuts and sews cloth and fur into clothes, makes hats and hose, and deals in used clothes.
Vocations.Lore: Dress is rank made visible, and laws say who may wear what, so the tailor knows everyone's true standing and debts. Most people wear clothes second or third hand; the old-clothes dealer is as common as the tailor. A sedentary trade, mocked as unmanly and feared as gossip.

Vocations.Name: Jeweller

Variants.Name: goldsmith
Variants.Description: Works gold at a bench by a small furnace: casts, hammers, solders and sets stones, for rings, chains and cups. A fine scale and a strongbox.
Variants.Lore: The goldsmith keeps other people's plate and lends against it, and so became the first banker. The street of the goldsmiths is the best guarded in a city.

Variants.Name: silversmith
Variants.Description: Raises cups, bowls and plate from sheets of silver with hammers over stakes, and chases them with patterns.
Variants.Lore: A household's plate is its savings: melted in a bad year and made again in a good one. The silversmith has seen the same cups three times.

Variants.Name: gem cutter
Variants.Description: Cuts and polishes facets on gems against a turning wheel dressed with grit, with the stone glued to a stick.
Variants.Lore: One wrong stroke halves the price. Dwarves read a rough stone's flaws at a glance and will not cut one in a hurry for any king.

Variants.Name: lapidary
Variants.Description: Knows, sorts, shapes and deals in stones: rounds and polishes them, carves seals and cameos, and tells true from false.
Variants.Lore: The books of stones give each a virtue: amethyst against drink, sapphire against poison. The lapidary sells the virtue with the stone and does not vouch for it.

Variants.Name: engraver
Variants.Description: Cuts lines into metal with a sharp steel point: letters, arms and ornament on plate, seals and dies. Works with a lens.
Variants.Lore: The one who cuts the ruler's seal can forge the ruler's word. An old seal is broken before witnesses, and the engraver is watched.

Variants.Name: enameller
Variants.Description: Fills cells in metal with powdered coloured glass and fires it until it melts into bright enamel.
Variants.Lore: Colours that do not fade in a thousand years. The recipes are kept in the family, and a daughter's husband is chosen for his hands.

Variants.Name: moneyer
Variants.Description: Strikes coin for the ruler: sets a blank of metal between two dies and hits it with a hammer. Works under guard and under oath.
Variants.Lore: A moneyer who strikes light coin loses the hand that struck it. The dies are locked up each night, and the moneyers with them, some say.

Variants.Name: assayer
Variants.Description: Tests the fineness of gold and silver with a touchstone, acid and a small furnace, and stamps what passes.
Variants.Lore: The ruler's coin is tried once a year in public. Gnomes and Lanternkin are hired as assayers because neither is thought to care about gold.

Variants.Name: ivory carver
Variants.Description: Carves tusk and tooth into combs, caskets, small figures and the handles of fine knives, with saws, files and fine blades.
Variants.Lore: Sunlander carvers serve the palace, and the king has the first tusk of every elephant. The Hoarkin carve walrus tooth through the dark half of the year.

Variants.Name: coral carver
Variants.Description: Cuts and polishes branches of red coral into beads, charms and small figures.
Variants.Lore: A branch of coral is hung on a child's neck in the south before it is given a name.

Variants.Name: amber worker
Variants.Description: Turns and polishes golden amber into beads for prayer strings, and into pendants and inlays.
Variants.Lore: The Amberbloods say amber is the blood of their oldest dead and will not see it cut into beads. They buy what they can and bury it.

Vocations.Description: Works precious metal, stones and ivory: makes plate, rings and reliquaries, cuts gems, strikes coin, and tests the fineness of metal.
Vocations.Lore: The richest of the crafts and the nearest to banking: the goldsmith keeps other people's treasure and strikes the ruler's coin. Trusted with wealth, so bound by the hardest oaths and the longest terms of office. Fantasy twists: gems that hold a spell, coin that cannot be clipped, a people that reads a stone's flaws at a glance.

Vocations.Name: Artist

Variants.Name: painter
Variants.Description: Paints panels and walls with pigments ground on a stone slab and bound with egg or oil: holy figures, portraits and arms. A stained smock and a handful of brushes.
Variants.Lore: Paid by the foot and by the price of the blue. The contract names how much gold and how many figures, and whether the master must paint the faces himself.

Variants.Name: sculptor
Variants.Description: Carves figures in stone with a mallet and chisels or models them in clay for casting. A yard of half-finished statues, white with dust.
Variants.Lore: A patron wants his own face on the saint. The sculptor gives the devil the face of whoever was slow to pay.

Variants.Name: image carver
Variants.Description: Carves holy images and altarpieces in wood, which are then painted and gilded.
Variants.Lore: When the faith turns, the images burn first. A carver learns to work for the next temple without comment.

Variants.Name: illuminator
Variants.Description: Paints the pictures, borders and great initials of books with tiny brushes, bright colours and gold leaf.
Variants.Lore: In the margins the hares hunt the hounds and the snails joust with knights. Nobody asked the illuminator for that, and nobody has stopped it.

Variants.Name: glass painter
Variants.Description: Paints faces, folds and letters on coloured glass and fires them in, for temple windows.
Variants.Lore: Light through the glass is the nearest most people come to seeing paradise. The donor is painted in at the bottom, small, with his arms.

Variants.Name: temple sculptor
Variants.Description: Carves the gods, dancers and beasts that cover a temple from base to tower, working on the stone in place, on a scaffold, for a lifetime.
Variants.Lore: Rainkeeper sculptors are born into the work and carve one temple for five generations. The last of them sees it finished and the first is carved on it.

Variants.Name: mosaic maker
Variants.Description: Sets small cubes of stone and coloured glass in wet plaster to make pictures on floors, walls and vaults.
Variants.Lore: The craft of the Old Realms, half lost. The best floors left are in ruins, and farmers plough up the cubes.

Variants.Name: map engraver
Variants.Description: Draws coasts, roads and towns from the reports of travellers and cuts them into copper or wood for printing. Works with compass, lens and fine tools.
Variants.Lore: Gnome maps are exact, and so rulers forbid their sale. Each engraver puts in one false village, to catch those who copy.

Variants.Name: instrument maker
Variants.Description: Makes instruments of music: harps, lutes, fiddles, pipes and drums, of thin wood, gut and horn.
Variants.Lore: An Elven harp takes forty years of seasoning and is strung for one player. When the player dies it is unstrung, and hung in a tree.

Vocations.Description: Makes images and ornaments: paints, carves and gilds for temples, courts and rich houses.
Vocations.Lore: A craftsman, not a genius: the painter belongs to a guild, often the saddlers' or the apothecaries', and is paid by the foot. Work is to order, for a patron who sets the subject. Only at a court does an artist gain a name. Fantasy twists: portraits that age for the sitter, statues that watch.

Vocations.Name: Artificer

Variants.Name: clockmaker
Variants.Description: Builds clocks of iron and brass wheels driven by weights, for towers and rich houses, and keeps them running.
Variants.Lore: A town clock is the council's pride and its standing quarrel with the temple bell. Gnomes made the first, and still set the others by theirs.

Variants.Name: fine locksmith
Variants.Description: Makes locks with hidden keyholes, false wards and traps, and strongboxes that only their owner can open.
Variants.Lore: Dwarven vault locks need three keys and three families. The smith who makes one keeps no drawing and takes an oath on it.

Variants.Name: instrument maker
Variants.Description: Makes instruments of measure in brass: astrolabes, sundials, compasses, scales and dividers, engraved with fine scales.
Variants.Lore: The Gnomes built the instruments of the sorcerer-kings and saw what was done with them. Since then they sell to anyone, and to no one alone.

Variants.Name: lens grinder
Variants.Description: Grinds and mounts lenses in tubes and frames for far-seeing and near-seeing glasses, and tests them against the stars.
Variants.Lore: The first far-seeing glass was offered to a prince for war. The Widegaze laughed at it, and then bought a dozen.

Variants.Name: tinker
Variants.Description: Travels with a pack of tools and a small brazier, and mends pots, pans, locks and anything of metal at the door.
Variants.Lore: Welcome and suspected at every door. Gnome tinkers carry news between the warrens in a speech of their own, and mend the pot while they do it.

Variants.Name: automaton maker
Variants.Description: Builds figures that move by springs, weights and water, and where there is magic, by a spell: singing birds, striking knights and walking servants.
Variants.Lore: The sorcerer-kings had servants of brass, and some are still found, standing in ruins. Nobody has made their like again, and the makers who try are watched.

Variants.Name: siege engineer
Variants.Description: Designs and builds the engines of a siege: trebuchets, rams, towers and mines. Works from drawings and commands carpenters.
Variants.Lore: Paid more than the captain and hated by both sides. A trebuchet is given a name, and it is always a woman's.

Variants.Name: object enchanter
Variants.Description: Binds a spell into a made thing, a ring, a blade or a lamp, with engraved signs, set stones and long ritual. A bench that is half a smith's and half a mage's.
Variants.Lore: A college licenses each enchantment and keeps a register of where it went. An unregistered ring is a crime twice over: once for the maker, once for the wearer.

Vocations.Description: Makes mechanisms and instruments, and in a world with magic, devices that hold it.
Vocations.Lore: The fantasy vocation with the thinnest historical root: the makers of clocks, scales and locks, who were few and admired. In a fantasy world the artificer stands between the smith and the mage, and is distrusted by both guilds. Patents and secrets are the trade's whole capital. Typical conflicts: a device that puts a craft out of work, a commission from a ruler that cannot be refused.

Vocations.Name: Merchant

Variants.Name: long-distance merchant
Variants.Description: Trades between lands, by ship and caravan, in goods worth their weight: spice, silk, furs and dyes. Richly dressed, travel-worn, and speaks several tongues.
Variants.Lore: Saltroad folk carry salt one way and gold the other and have kin at both ends. A caravan's books are kept in a script only the family reads.

Variants.Name: wholesaler
Variants.Description: Buys by the shipload and sells by the bale from a warehouse, and never from a stall.
Variants.Lore: Accused of buying up the market before it opens, which is a crime with three names. The warehouse is where the town's food is, and everyone knows it.

Variants.Name: draper
Variants.Description: Deals in woollen cloth by the bolt and measures it with a yard rod on a long counter.
Variants.Lore: The drapers sit on the council in every cloth town. The weavers who make the cloth do not, and remember it.

Variants.Name: mercer
Variants.Description: Deals in silk, velvet, fine linen and the small costly wares of dress: ribbons, laces and thread of gold.
Variants.Lore: The richest of the guilds in most cities, and the one that lends to kings. A mercer's daughter is a match for a poor knight, and both know it.

Variants.Name: spicer
Variants.Description: Deals in pepper, ginger, saffron, sugar and drugs, weighed out on small scales from rows of jars and chests.
Variants.Lore: Pepper was counted out by the corn and taken as rent. The spicers put it about that it grows guarded by serpents, to explain the price.

Variants.Name: grain factor
Variants.Description: Buys grain from the country and sells it to the town, and holds it in granaries against the price. Blamed in every hungry year.
Variants.Lore: The first house a mob visits in a hungry year. Dwarves, who keep seven years of grain behind the gate, do not sell in the seventh.

Variants.Name: broker
Variants.Description: Brings buyer and seller together for a fee, owns no goods, and knows every price in the market.
Variants.Lore: Sworn to serve both sides and suspected of serving himself. A stranger may only buy in a town through a licensed one.

Variants.Name: moneychanger
Variants.Description: Sits at a bench with scales and piles of coin, and changes one money into another for a cut.
Variants.Lore: Gnomes can tell a clipped coin by its ring on the bench. The word for a bank is the word for that bench, and a broken bench means a failed changer.

Variants.Name: banker
Variants.Description: Takes deposits, makes loans and writes letters of credit that are paid in a distant city. A counting house with ledgers and an iron chest.
Variants.Lore: Lanternkin bankers seal a debt with a vial of their own blood, which glows while they live. A house is trusted for as long as its vials shine.

Variants.Name: moneylender
Variants.Description: Lends coin against a pledge or a written bond and takes interest. Needed by all and loved by none.
Variants.Lore: Every faith forbids usury and every lord needs a loan. So the trade falls to strangers, who are protected until the debt is due and expelled after.

Variants.Name: insurer
Variants.Description: Takes a fee to bear the risk of a ship or a cargo, and pays if it is lost. Works at a table near the harbour, with contracts and news of every sailing.
Variants.Lore: A new trade of the sea ports. The news of a wreck is worth money for an hour, and the insurers pay the fastest riders.

Vocations.Description: Buys in one place and sells in another, in bulk and over distance, and lends, changes and insures money.
Vocations.Lore: The estate that fits no estate: neither fights, prays nor ploughs, and grows richer than those who do. Merchants rule the towns through their guild and buy their way into the nobility within three generations. Usury is a sin they pay the temple to forgive. Fantasy twists: houses that trade between peoples who cannot meet, contracts witnessed by something that enforces them.

Vocations.Name: Shopkeeper

Variants.Name: retailer
Variants.Description: Keeps a shop on the ground floor of the house, with a shutter that folds down into a counter, and sells by the piece and the ounce.
Variants.Lore: The guild fixes what a shop may sell and when it may open. A shop lit after curfew is fined, and the fine is paid by all of them.

Variants.Name: stallholder
Variants.Description: Sells from a trestle table under an awning on the market square, on the days the market is held.
Variants.Lore: A pitch on the square is inherited and fought over by the foot. The same family has stood under the same arch for two hundred years.

Variants.Name: huckster
Variants.Description: Buys small lots at dawn and sells them dearer through the day from a basket or a tray: eggs, fruit, fish and candles. Often a woman.
Variants.Lore: Fined every week for selling dear what she bought cheap that morning. The fine is the town's oldest tax, and nobody means it to stop her.

Variants.Name: pedlar
Variants.Description: Walks from village to village with a pack on the back, full of needles, ribbons, knives and news.
Variants.Lore: Brings needles, ribbons and the news of three valleys. Every village thinks the pedlar a spy, and every lord has used one.

Variants.Name: chapman
Variants.Description: A travelling dealer with a packhorse or a cart, who sells small wares and buys what the country has to sell.
Variants.Lore: Sells the ballads and the cheap books as well as the pins. What the country knows of the world, it knows from the chapman.

Variants.Name: market trader
Variants.Description: Follows the round of weekly markets and yearly fairs with a cart of goods and a folding stall.
Variants.Lore: At a fair the traders have their own court, which sits at once and judges before the dust has settled on their feet.

Vocations.Description: Sells small quantities to those who live near: from a stall, a shop or a pack.
Vocations.Lore: The small end of trade, mostly poor and often a woman. Hucksters buy at dawn and sell dearer by noon, and are fined for it every week. The pedlar carries needles, ribbons and news to places no merchant visits, and is welcome and suspected in equal parts.

Vocations.Name: Carter

Variants.Name: carter
Variants.Description: Drives a two-wheeled cart behind a horse or an ox, walking beside it with a whip. A smock, a hood and muddy boots.
Variants.Lore: Knows every inn, rut and toll for forty miles. Carters carry letters and gossip for nothing, and are trusted with neither.

Variants.Name: teamster
Variants.Description: Drives a heavy four-wheeled wagon behind a team of four or six, and can back it through a gate.
Variants.Lore: Speaks to the team in a language of his own. The lead horse wears the bells, and a teamster who needs help on a hill forfeits them.

Variants.Name: muleteer
Variants.Description: Leads a string of loaded mules over tracks no cart can pass, with bells on the lead animal.
Variants.Lore: Swears more than any other trade and is forgiven it, since mules understand nothing else. The mountain roads have no other traffic.

Variants.Name: caravan driver
Variants.Description: Walks or rides with a line of camels or other pack animals across desert and steppe, robed and veiled against sun and dust.
Variants.Lore: Saltroad folk walk beside the camel rather than tire it. On the worst stretches they travel by night and are led by Duskreader guides.

Variants.Name: caravan master
Variants.Description: Commands a caravan: chooses the way and the wells, deals with tolls and guards, and answers for every bale.
Variants.Lore: On the road the master is judge and lord, and a prince travelling with the caravan obeys. A master who loses a well loses his name.

Variants.Name: drover
Variants.Description: Drives herds of cattle, sheep or geese on foot over long distances to market, with dogs and a staff.
Variants.Lore: Licensed and bonded, because he is trusted with a district's wealth on the hoof. He carries the money home, so drovers became bankers of a kind.

Variants.Name: porter
Variants.Description: Carries loads on the back, with a frame, a strap across the forehead or a knot on the shoulder, through streets and up stairs.
Variants.Lore: The porters' guild holds the quay or the gate by right, and nothing moves that they have not carried. Orcs hold the trade in many ports.

Variants.Name: water carrier
Variants.Description: Carries water from the fountain or the river to the houses, in two pails on a yoke or in a skin on the back.
Variants.Lore: The poorest honest trade in a city. At a fire the water carriers are pressed into service, and paid after, if at all.

Variants.Name: courier
Variants.Description: Carries letters and small parcels on foot or on horseback, with a satchel, a staff and the badge of the sender.
Variants.Lore: A courier's person is safe by custom in every land. Swiftborn runners are the fastest, and spend their short years on the road gladly.

Variants.Name: post rider
Variants.Description: Rides fast from one post house to the next and changes horses at each, with a horn and a sealed bag.
Variants.Lore: The Old Realms kept a horse every ten miles. A few kingdoms keep the posts still, and their kings hear the news a week before their neighbours.

Variants.Name: elephant driver
Variants.Description: Sits on the neck of an elephant and guides it with the feet, the voice and a hooked goad, to haul timber, carry loads or bear a lord.
Variants.Lore: Among the Rainkeepers a driver is given to one elephant as a boy, and the two grow old together. An elephant mourns its driver, and may refuse another.

Vocations.Description: Moves goods and messages by land: with cart, pack animal or his own back.
Vocations.Lore: Rough men of the road who know every inn, toll and ford. Caravan masters are trusted with fortunes; porters are the poorest free men in a town. The road has its own law, and its own tolls, bandits and guides. Fantasy twists: beasts of burden no stable could hold, roads that are only open at certain hours.

Vocations.Name: Sailor

Variants.Name: seaman
Variants.Description: Works a ship before the mast: hauls ropes, climbs the rigging, rows and bails. Barefoot, in loose trousers, with a knife on a lanyard.
Variants.Lore: Paid by a share of the voyage, in most waters, and has a vote on whether to throw the cargo overboard in a storm.

Variants.Name: ship's master
Variants.Description: Commands a ship and answers for the vessel, the cargo and the crew. Stands at the stern, in a good coat, by the steering oar.
Variants.Lore: Often a part owner, and by the sea law the judge, the priest and the notary on board. The law also says when the crew may refuse him.

Variants.Name: pilot
Variants.Description: Knows one coast or river mouth by heart, its bars, rocks and tides, and guides ships through it with a sounding lead.
Variants.Lore: A pilot who loses a ship on his own bar answers for it with his head, by the old sea laws. Shoalfolk pilots see the reef through the water.

Variants.Name: rigger
Variants.Description: Fits and mends the ropes and spars of a ship, splices and knots, and works aloft without fear.
Variants.Lore: Boughwalkers and Catfolk go aloft without a thought and are hired on every ship that can get them.

Variants.Name: bargeman
Variants.Description: Works a flat barge down a river or along a canal, with a pole, a sweep or a tow horse on the bank.
Variants.Lore: Halfling bargemen live aboard with the family, the hens and a garden in tubs, and know every lock-keeper's birthday.

Variants.Name: boatman
Variants.Description: Rows or poles a small boat for hire, carrying people and goods about a harbour or a town of canals.
Variants.Lore: In the cities of the Canal folk the boatmen hear every quarrel and every courtship in the town, and sing over them.

Variants.Name: ferryman
Variants.Description: Carries travellers, carts and beasts across one river at one place, on a flat boat hauled along a rope or rowed.
Variants.Lore: Owns the crossing by an old right and is paid by all, the dead included: in many lands a coin is put in the mouth of a corpse for him.

Variants.Name: raftsman
Variants.Description: Rides rafts of logs lashed together down a river to the sawmills and the sea, steering with long sweeps.
Variants.Lore: The raft is the cargo. The raftsmen ride it for weeks, sell it at the river mouth and walk home.

Variants.Name: ship's lookout
Variants.Description: Stands in the top of the mast and watches for land, rocks, weather and sails, and calls down what is seen.
Variants.Lore: A Widegaze in the top sees nearly the whole horizon at once, and a master who has sailed with one will not sail without.

Vocations.Description: Works a vessel: on the sea, on a river, on a lake or a canal.
Vocations.Lore: A people apart, with their own speech, pay by share and long absences. Half of every port is waiting for a ship. Pilots are licensed and guard their knowledge of the bar and the channel. The ferryman owns his crossing by right and is paid by all. Fantasy twists: winds that are bought, a people that sees the reef through the water.

Vocations.Name: Innkeeper

Variants.Name: innkeeper
Variants.Description: Keeps a house with beds, a hall and a stable yard on a road or in a town. Stands at the door in an apron, with a ring of keys.
Variants.Lore: A stranger must lodge at an inn by law, and the host answers for the guest's goods and for the guest. He is the first to be questioned and the last to have seen anything.

Variants.Name: taverner
Variants.Description: Sells wine by the cup and the jug in a cellar or a ground-floor room with benches, and keeps the tally in chalk.
Variants.Lore: The tavern is the poor man's hall. The watch looks in at curfew, and the taverner's score in chalk is evidence in court.

Variants.Name: hosteller
Variants.Description: Keeps a hostel for pilgrims, merchants or students of one town or one faith, with plain beds in a common room.
Variants.Lore: Each nation of merchants has its own house in a foreign port, with its own cook and its own law inside the door.

Variants.Name: alehouse keeper
Variants.Description: Sells ale in the front room of a small house, with a bush or a broom on a pole over the door.
Variants.Lore: Mostly a widow, and the alehouse is her pension. The village's quarrels are started and settled on her bench.

Variants.Name: cookshop keeper
Variants.Description: Feeds travellers and lodgers from a common pot and a spit in the kitchen of an inn or a house on the road.
Variants.Lore: Halfling innkeepers are judged on the table before the beds, and a traveller plans the road by their kitchens.

Variants.Name: bathhouse keeper
Variants.Description: Keeps a bathhouse with wooden tubs, hot stones and steam, where people wash, are shaved and bled, eat and meet.
Variants.Lore: The bathhouse has a worse name than the tavern and more custom. Every plague closes it and every council opens it again.

Variants.Name: stable keeper
Variants.Description: Keeps a yard with stalls, hay and a trough, where travellers leave their animals and hire fresh ones.
Variants.Lore: Sells horses on the side, and no one has trusted a horse dealer since the Dawn. He knows who rode in at night, and from where.

Vocations.Description: Keeps a house where strangers eat, drink, sleep, wash and stable their animals.
Vocations.Lore: The host knows who came, with what and with whom, and is by turns informer, banker, broker and fence. An inn is where a stranger must lodge by law, and where a deal is witnessed. The tavern is the common room of the poor; the bathhouse has a worse name.

Vocations.Name: Healer

Variants.Name: physician
Variants.Description: A learned healer in a long gown and a cap, who studies the patient's urine in a glass flask, reads the pulse and the stars, and prescribes.
Variants.Lore: Reads the stars and the urine and never touches a knife. A physician is paid whether the patient lives or not, and the patients have noticed.

Variants.Name: surgeon
Variants.Description: Cuts, stitches, sets and burns: treats wounds, breaks, stones and growths with knives, saws, needles and hot irons.
Variants.Lore: The Flinchless became the world's surgeons: a people that feels no pain learnt early to look for every wound, and to keep a steady hand.

Variants.Name: barber-surgeon
Variants.Description: Shaves and cuts hair, and also lets blood, pulls teeth and dresses wounds. A striped pole and a basin at the door.
Variants.Lore: Travels with armies and learns more in one battle than a physician in a library. The red on the pole is the blood and the white the bandage.

Variants.Name: barber
Variants.Description: Shaves beards and cuts hair with a razor, shears, a comb and a basin of hot water, in a shop full of talk.
Variants.Lore: The barber's shop is where a town's news is combed out. A ruler who trusts a man with a razor at his throat tells him things.

Variants.Name: bonesetter
Variants.Description: Sets broken bones and puts joints back by hand, with splints and bandages. A strong grip, learnt in the family and not from books.
Variants.Lore: A gift that runs in families, and the college of physicians would like it stopped. People go to the bonesetter first all the same.

Variants.Name: tooth puller
Variants.Description: Pulls teeth in the market place with pliers, before a crowd, with a string of teeth round the neck as a sign.
Variants.Lore: Works at fairs with a drummer, to cover the noise. The proverb for a liar is that he lies like one.

Variants.Name: midwife
Variants.Description: Helps women in childbirth, with warm oil, clean linen, a birthing stool and long practice. Trusted with the secrets of every house.
Variants.Lore: May christen a child that will not live, and so is licensed by the temple. She knows whose child is whose, and is feared for it.

Variants.Name: nurse
